algorithm: autoregressive next-token prediction over discretized MANO motion tokens (Grouped Residual Quantization) for pretraining; L1-loss MLP regression head over learnable query tokens for post-training imitation learning
hand: 6-DoF Inspire hand mounted on a 7-DoF Franka Research 3 arm (real robot); MANO parametric hand model used as the pretraining representation (no physical hardware)
success_criterion: "strict binary criteria (e.g., complete lid closure, accurate toy placement)", each task evaluated over 20 randomized trials with varied initial object positions
headline_metric: success rate on 7 real-world dexterous manipulation tasks (Table 7, 20 trials/task)
headline_value: Being-H0 65-100% across tasks (e.g. 100% Pour-Cup, 85% Close-Toolbox, 75% Unfold-Clothes, 60% Close-Lid) vs. GR00T N1.5 40-90% and InternVL3 25-55% under identical post-training data
human_data: UniHand (11 aggregated benchmarks, >440K task trajectories, >130M frames, >1,100 hours, >165M generated motion-instruction pairs; a balanced 2.5M-sample subset UniHand-2.5M used for pretraining)
paper_code_mismatch: The actual downstream action-head module referenced in §4.3 (learnable query tokens, proprioceptive projector f_p, regression head f_r) is not present in the parsed code; the repo's own TODO list marks 'Training code and scripts' as unreleased, so the action-chunk-length=16 value and exact proprioception-vector fields come only from inference/eval CLI examples, not a verifiable implementation.
note_gaps: Exact proprioception vector fields for post-training are not itemized in the paper text and cannot be confirmed from code; tokenizer loss equations are rendered as unextracted images in the source markdown, so only the weighted-combination description (λ1=0.02, λ2=1.0) is quotable, not the full formula.
backbone: InternVL3 architecture (InternViT-300M visual encoder + 2-layer MLP projector, LLM decoder InternLM3/Qwen2.5), trained at three scales
action_head: post-training: lightweight MLP regression head (f_r) over a set of learnable query tokens attending to the pretrained VLA encoder's context, trained with an L1 imitation-learning loss to produce end-effector poses and dexterous hand joint positions; pretraining uses a separate discrete Grouped Residual Quantization (GRQ) tokenizer (part-level wrist/finger token streams) to generate MANO hand-motion tokens autoregressively
pretrain_data: UniHand — 11 aggregated human-video benchmark sources, >440K task trajectories, >130M frames, >1,100 hours, >165M generated motion-instruction pairs; a balanced 2.5M-sample subset (UniHand-2.5M) used for pretraining
dexterous_evidence: "Our experiments are conducted using a hardware setup including a 7-DoF Franka Research 3 arm, a 6-DoF Inspire hand, and a RealSense L515 camera for RGB streaming." (§6.1.3, "Robot System")
